picks.title: University Presses Sign Charter Promising Integrity, Vigilance Over AI
picks.rationale: New concrete event: 100+ scholarly publishers from 26 countries sign a six-point charter committing to responsible AI. Separate from the 11-04 Meridian licensing story.
picks.excerpt: More than 100 scholarly publishers from 26 countries, including 27 from the U.S., signed a six-point charter committing to quality, transparency and 'responsible approaches to artificial intelligence.'

picks.title: Pathfinder publisher disputes claims of AI art in its latest book, Feybound
picks.rationale: Fresh (11-12) AI-art dispute over a published sourcebook. Paizo bans AI art and rejects the fan claims. Shows how illustration provenance is now policed in print publishing.
picks.excerpt: Paizo, which bans AI art in its TTRPG books, rejects fan claims that AI-generated illustrations slipped into its new Pathfinder sourcebook Feybound.

picks.title: [스타트업-ing] "AI가 초벌 번역, 사람이 완성"…하이브마인드, '오로라 번역 서포터즈' 출범
picks.rationale: New launch of a hybrid workflow: generative AI does the first-pass translation and human translators finish it. A concrete production model for content translation.
picks.excerpt: 콘텐츠 번역사 하이브마인드가 생성형 AI 초벌 번역을 사람이 다듬는 '오로라 번역 서포터즈'를 출범했다. 맥락·정서가 중요한 콘텐츠 번역 품질이 목표다.

picks.title: Libraries, Publishers, and the Users We Both Serve
picks.rationale: Practical argument that libraries and publishers should study how users actually work with AI research tools. Fresh (11-10) and not covered by earlier Scholarly Kitchen cards.
picks.excerpt: Libraries and publishers can claim agency in the AI age by again studying in depth how their users actually work with AI research tools.

picks.title: Copyright Infringement Lawsuit Against OpenAI Draws More than 50 (Very Illuminating) Amicus Briefs
picks.rationale: The orchestrator assigned this to books only. It maps all 50+ amicus filings in In re OpenAI, most of them never carded (only the publishers' and unions' briefs ran before).
picks.excerpt: More than 50 amicus briefs filed in In re OpenAI map the fault lines of the most closely watched AI copyright case.
